interface.cleanup: deferRelease callbacks run in reverse registration order, once; errors are generic package/code records and all other cleanups continue.

boundaries: Only explicitly already-imported trusted local descriptors are accepted; this function does not import a model-supplied path, install packages, fetch remote code, or grant tool permissions.

Selected module bytes are reread through a nonsymlink file and checked against contentSha256. The hash is not a signed supply-chain guarantee and does not fingerprint dependency closures or mutable JavaScript closure state.
Bindings omit sourceUrl and local paths. Resume callers must pass expectedBindings to compare exact ordered package pins before activation.

Metadata and selected function references are copied/frozen; separate activations select later versions without rebinding earlier Runs. Caller must retain resources until its Run settles, then release. This is not hot-unload or an execution sandbox.

Activation is atomic with respect to contributions exposed by this API, not arbitrary effects of trusted JavaScript. Resource owners must register cleanup immediately through deferRelease. Synchronous runaway code and noncooperative resource callbacks are not forcibly terminated.
Skill metadata alone does not mean loaded or adopted. The two authored example packages expose ordinary methodResult tools so actual reads enter the existing acquired-method owner.
The existing explicit-function extension path remains unchanged. Offline fixtures prove Runtime integration, not market facts or semantic quality.
The listed hashes pin plugin-owned source/test inputs; final stage evidence must separately pin the complete Runtime/Host dependency closure. These focused checks are not a full candidate regression.
